clues.text: I was a Persian king.
I ruled over 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia.
I made Esther queen instead of Vashti.
I promoted Haman the Agagite above the other princes.
I ordered Haman hanged on his own stake.
I sat on my royal throne in Shushan the citadel.
In the third year of my reign I held a great banquet for my princes.
Queen Vashti refused to come at my order.
I held out the golden scepter to Esther.
I told Esther that even to the half of my kingdom, her request would be granted.
I could not sleep, so the book of historical records was read to me.
I asked what honor had been given to Mordecai for saving my life.
I gave Haman's house to Queen Esther.
I gave Mordecai the signet ring I had taken from Haman.
I showed the wealth of my glorious kingdom for 180 days.
I consulted seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to me.
I sent letters that every husband should be master in his own house.
In the seventh year of my reign I put the royal headdress on Esther.
I proclaimed an amnesty for the provinces at Esther's banquet.
I removed my signet ring and gave it to Haman for use against the Jews.
I ordered Haman to honor Mordecai with royal attire and the horse I ride.
When I saw Haman on Esther's couch, I exclaimed.
I told Esther and Mordecai to write in my name for the Jews and seal it with my ring.
At the beginning of my reign, enemies wrote an accusation against Judah and Jerusalem.
I imposed forced labor on the land and the islands of the sea.
I deposed Vashti in my third year and crowned Esther in my seventh
I first sealed Haman's decree to annihilate the Jews, then authorized Mordecai's counter-decree that could not be revoked.
After sleepless reading of the records, I made Haman parade the Jew who had exposed a plot against me.
My mighty acts and Mordecai's greatness were written in the book of the history of the times of the kings of Media and Persia.
I was a king of Persia in the days of Ezra and Nehemiah.
Nehemiah was cupbearer to me.
I sent Nehemiah to Judah to rebuild the city.
I granted Ezra everything he requested.
I issued an order that willing Israelites could go with Ezra to Jerusalem.
Enemies wrote to me accusing the Jews of rebuilding a rebellious city.
After an investigation, I ordered the work in Jerusalem to stop until I issued another order.
I gave Ezra a letter as priest and copyist of the Law of the God of the heavens.
I sent Ezra with my seven advisers to investigate whether God's Law was being applied in Judah and Jerusalem.
I said the expenses for Jehovah's house could come from the royal treasury.
I ordered the treasurers Beyond the River to give Ezra whatever he requested, promptly.
When Nehemiah looked gloomy, I asked what he was seeking.
With my royal consort beside me, I asked how long Nehemiah's journey would be.
I told Rehum and Shimshai that powerful kings once ruled from Jerusalem over the region Beyond the River.
I warned Rehum and Shimshai not to neglect stopping the work, so my interests would not be harmed.
I forbade tax, tribute, or toll on priests, Levites, musicians, doorkeepers, temple servants, and workers of God's house.
I authorized Ezra to appoint magistrates and judges Beyond the River for those who knew God's laws.
I said judgment for breaking God's Law or the king's law could be death, banishment, a fine, or imprisonment.
I gave Nehemiah letters for the governors Beyond the River and for Asaph, keeper of the Royal Park.
I also sent army chiefs and horsemen with Nehemiah.
From my 20th year to my 32nd year, Nehemiah served as governor in Judah.
In my 32nd year, Nehemiah came back to me, then later asked leave to return to Jerusalem.
I ordered rebuilding in Jerusalem halted, but I also sent Ezra with silver, gold, and authority concerning Jehovah's house.
My cupbearer Nehemiah asked for timber for the Fortress of the House and the city walls, and I gave him the letters.
Ezra praised Jehovah because I was moved to beautify Jehovah's house in Jerusalem and showed him loyal love before my advisers and princes.
The elders finished Jehovah's house by the order of the God of Israel and by the order of Cyrus, Darius, and me.
I capped Ezra's supplies at 100 talents of silver, 100 cor of wheat, 100 bath of wine, 100 bath of oil, and salt without limit.
I was a companion of Daniel in Babylon.
With Hananiah and Mishael, I refused to worship the image of gold.
King Nebuchadnezzar had me and two others thrown into the burning fiery furnace.
Together with Hananiah and Mishael, I stepped out of the fire unharmed.
I was among youths from the tribe of Judah taken for the king's service.
The principal court official also gave me a Babylonian name.
For ten days, my companions and I ate vegetables and drank water instead of the king's delicacies.
At Daniel's request, Nebuchadnezzar appointed me over the administration of the province of Babylon.
Some Chaldeans accused me before Nebuchadnezzar of refusing his image.
My two companions and I told Nebuchadnezzar that we had no need to answer him in that matter.
My companions and I said that even if our God did not rescue us, we would not worship the King's image.
After three years of training, Nebuchadnezzar found no one like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and me.
In matters of wisdom, Nebuchadnezzar found my companions and me ten times better than his magic-practicing priests and conjurers.
When the wise men were to be killed, Daniel informed me and my companions and asked us to pray for mercy.
Mighty men from the king's army bound me and my companions and threw us into the furnace still wearing our clothes.
The furnace was heated seven times hotter than usual because of me and my companions.
Not a hair of my head was singed, and there was not even the smell of fire on me.
I answered Nebuchadnezzar along with Hananiah and Mishael that our God could rescue us from the furnace and from his hand.
The men who took my companions and me up to the furnace were killed by the flames, but we fell bound into the fire and later walked out free.
After the fire had no effect on my body or cloaks, Nebuchadnezzar promoted me and my companions again in the province of Babylon.
From Judah's youths in the palace school to administrators of Babylon, I stood with Hananiah and Mishael against the golden image on the plain of Dura.
Daniel asked that I be set over Babylon's administration; later Nebuchadnezzar's officials saw that the fire had not touched me.
I was Jeremiah's secretary.
I wrote Jehovah's words in a scroll at Jeremiah's dictation.
I read aloud from the scroll at the house of Jehovah.
King Jehoiakim burned the scroll I had written.
I was the son of Neriah.
Jeremiah called me when he could not enter Jehovah's house, and sent me to read the scroll on a fast day.
I read in Gemariah's chamber in the upper courtyard, at the entrance of the new gate.
The princes sent Jehudi to bring me and the scroll, and I read it to them.
I told the princes Jeremiah dictated the words and I wrote them with ink in the scroll.
The princes told me to hide, myself and Jeremiah, and not let anyone know where we were.
Jehoiakim ordered men to seize me and Jeremiah, but Jehovah kept us concealed.
After the first scroll was burned, Jeremiah gave me another scroll and I wrote the same words again, with many more added.
Jeremiah gave me the deed of purchase for the field in Anathoth.
Before witnesses, Jeremiah commanded me to put the sealed and unsealed deeds into an earthenware vessel.
My grandfather was Mahseiah.
I wrote the scroll in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah.
I read it in the fifth year of Jehoiakim, in the ninth month, during a proclaimed fast.
Men accused me of inciting Jeremiah against them so they would be handed over to the Chaldeans.
Johanan and the army chiefs took me and Jeremiah down to Egypt, as far as Tahpanhes.
Jehovah said I had groaned, “Woe to me,” weary and with no resting-place.
Jehovah told me to stop seeking great things for myself.
Jehovah promised that wherever I went, he would grant me my life as a spoil.
My brother Seraiah son of Neriah went with Zedekiah to Babylon as quartermaster.
I wrote Jeremiah's words, read them in the temple, then after the king burned that scroll I wrote a second scroll with still more words.
During Babylon's siege I stored Jeremiah's land deeds in earthenware for a long time, as Jehovah said fields would again be bought.
After Jerusalem fell, I was blamed for Jeremiah's message and forced into Egypt with him.
In Jehoiakim's fourth year, while I wrote the scroll, Jehovah answered my grief: calamity was coming, yet my life would be spared wherever I went.
I was a king of Babylon.
I held a great feast for a thousand of my nobles.
Fingers of a man's hand wrote on the plaster of my palace wall.
Daniel read the writing and told me its interpretation.
That very night I was killed.
Under the influence of wine, I ordered the gold and silver vessels from Jehovah's temple brought in.
My nobles, concubines, and secondary wives drank from those vessels with me.
While drinking, we praised gods of gold, silver, copper, iron, wood, and stone.
When I saw the hand writing, I turned pale and my knees knocked together.
I loudly summoned the conjurers, the Chaldeans, and the astrologers.
I promised purple clothing, a gold necklace, and third place in the kingdom to whoever read the writing.
My wise men could not read the writing or make known its interpretation.
The queen told me to summon Daniel, whom my father had named Belteshazzar.
I asked Daniel if he was of the exiles of Judah whom my father the king brought out of Judah.
I told Daniel he would rule as the third one in the kingdom if he interpreted the writing.
Daniel said I could keep my gifts and give my presents to others.
Daniel said I had not humbled my heart, though I knew what happened to Nebuchadnezzar my father.
Daniel said I had exalted myself against the Lord of the heavens and had not glorified the God in whose hand was my breath.
The writing against me was MENE, MENE, TEKEL, and PARSIN.
After the interpretation, I clothed Daniel with purple and put a gold necklace on him.
They heralded that Daniel was to become the third ruler in my kingdom.
I drank from the temple vessels while praising lifeless gods, then saw a hand write my judgment opposite the lampstand.
I offered third place in the kingdom for the interpretation; that same night my kingdom ended and I was killed.
Daniel weighed me as lacking and said my kingdom was divided and given to the Medes and the Persians, and Darius the Mede received it after me.
I was king of Persia.
I made a proclamation letting the Jews go up to rebuild Jehovah's house in Jerusalem.
Jehovah stirred my spirit to fulfill his word spoken by Jeremiah.
I said Jehovah the God of the heavens had given me all the kingdoms of the earth.
I brought out the utensils of Jehovah's house that Nebuchadnezzar had taken.
Jehovah called me his shepherd.
Jehovah called me his anointed one.
Jehovah said I would completely carry out all his will.
Jehovah said I would build his city and set his exiles free without a price or a bribe.
I put my proclamation in writing throughout my kingdom.
I commissioned the rebuilding of Jehovah's house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
I said neighbors should help the returning people with silver, gold, goods, and livestock.
I released the temple vessels under Mithredath the treasurer for Sheshbazzar the chieftain of Judah.
In my first year I ordered that the house of God in Jerusalem be rebuilt as a place for sacrifices.
Jehovah said he took hold of my right hand to subdue nations and open double doors before me.
Jehovah said he called me by name for the sake of Jacob his servant, though I did not know him.
I ordered the temple's height 60 cubits and width 60 cubits, with expenses from the king's house.
I ordered the gold and silver vessels returned to their place in the temple in Jerusalem.
I made Sheshbazzar governor and told him to deposit the vessels in the temple and rebuild that house.
Daniel remained until the first year of my kingship.
Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and during my reign as king.
In the third year of my kingship, a revelation was given to Daniel concerning a great conflict.
Advisers were hired against Judah's builders throughout my days until the reign of Darius.
Long before my decree, Jehovah named me as the shepherd who would say of Jerusalem that she would be rebuilt and of the temple that its foundation would be laid.
I proclaimed freedom for Jehovah's people and returned Nebuchadnezzar's looted temple vessels for Jehovah's house in Jerusalem.
Jews later told Persian officials that in my first year as king of Babylon I ordered God's house rebuilt and appointed Sheshbazzar.
Jehovah said he would go before me, break copper doors, and give me hidden treasures so I would know he is the God of Israel who called me by name.
My written decree for Jehovah's house was later found and confirmed under Darius, and the builders also worked by my order along with Darius and Artaxerxes.
I was thrown into a pit of lions.
My God sent his angel and shut the mouth of the lions.
I resolved not to defile myself with the king's delicacies or his wine.
I was among youths of Judah taken to serve in Babylon.
I made known both a king's dream and its interpretation.
I read mysterious writing on a palace wall and explained it.
Three times a day I got down on my knees and prayed.
I kept praying even after a royal ban forbade petitions to anyone but the king.
I told a king that God would set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed.
Jehovah held me up with Noah and Job as an example of righteousness.
I was lifted unharmed out of the lions' pit because I had trusted in my God.
Officials could find no negligence or corruption in me.
I asked to be tested for ten days on vegetables and water.
After ten days my appearance was better than those eating the king's delicacies.
The true God gave me understanding in all sorts of visions and dreams.
In matters of wisdom Nebuchadnezzar found me ten times better than his magic-practicing priests and conjurers.
I remained in Babylon until the first year of King Cyrus.
When Babylon's wise men faced death, I asked Nebuchadnezzar to grant me time.
I asked my companions to pray for mercy so God would reveal Nebuchadnezzar's dream.
Nebuchadnezzar's dream was revealed to me in a vision at night.
I said there is a God in the heavens who is a Revealer of secrets.
I described an immense image with a head of gold and feet of iron mixed with clay.
I said a stone cut not by hands struck the image and became a mountain filling the earth.
Nebuchadnezzar made me ruler over the province of Babylon and chief prefect over all the wise men.
At my request, Nebuchadnezzar appointed Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah over Babylon's administration.
I interpreted a dream about an enormous tree that was to be chopped down.
I urged a king to turn away from his sins by doing what is right and showing mercy to the poor.
I told Belshazzar he could keep his gifts; I would still read the writing.
I read the writing: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, and PARSIN.
I said a kingdom had been numbered, weighed, divided, and given to the Medes and the Persians.
I was one of three high officials under Darius the Mede.
Darius intended to elevate me over the entire kingdom.
My roof-chamber windows were open toward Jerusalem when I prayed.
A stone was placed over the entrance of the pit and sealed concerning me.
I told Darius I had done him no wrong.
I prospered in the kingdom of Darius and in the kingdom of Cyrus the Persian.
I was trained for three years before entering the king's service.
I was to be taught the writing and the language of the Chaldeans.
I spoke discreetly and cautiously to Arioch, chief of the king's bodyguard.
I told Nebuchadnezzar that his dream was not revealed to me because I had greater wisdom than anyone living.
Nebuchadnezzar fell facedown and paid homage to me after I revealed the secret.
I was alarmed for a moment when I grasped the meaning of the tree dream.
The queen recommended me when the wise men could not read the writing on the wall.
I told Belshazzar he had not humbled his heart, though he knew Nebuchadnezzar's fall.
I said Belshazzar had praised gods that see nothing, hear nothing, and know nothing.
Accusers said they would find no grounds against me unless against the law of my God.
In a night vision I saw four huge beasts come out of the sea.
I saw someone like a son of man coming with the clouds of the heavens.
I went near to one standing there to ask the true meaning of what I saw.
My spirit was distressed, and the visions of my head frightened me.
In vision I was in Shushan the citadel, next to the watercourse of Ulai.
I saw a two-horned ram and a male goat with a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
A voice called concerning me, “Gabriel, make that one understand what he saw.”
After the vision I felt exhausted and was sick for some days.
From Jeremiah's books I discerned 70 years for Jerusalem's desolation.
I entreated Jehovah with prayer, fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
While I was still praying, Gabriel came about the time of the evening gift offering.
I was told there are 70 weeks determined for my people and my holy city.
I was told that from the word to restore Jerusalem until Messiah the Leader there would be 7 weeks, also 62 weeks.
I mourned three full weeks; no rich food, meat, or wine entered my mouth.
On the bank of the Tigris I saw a man clothed in linen with a belt of gold from Uphaz.
Only I saw the vision; the men with me trembled and ran away to hide.
I was addressed as someone very precious.
I learned the prince of Persia opposed the messenger for 21 days until Michael helped.
I was told to keep the words secret and seal up the book until the time of the end.
I was told to go on to the end; I would rest and stand up for my lot at the end of the days.
Jesus pointed to a prophecy I wrote about the disgusting thing that causes desolation.
Jehovah used my wisdom as a measuring stick when rebuking a proud ruler of Tyre.
I refused royal delicacies as a youth and later refused royal gifts before announcing a king's doom.
I secured Babylon posts for three companions who later faced a furnace; I myself later faced lions for praying.
I explained successive kingdoms from a metal image, then saw four beasts representing kings rise from the sea.
I announced an everlasting God-set kingdom from the image dream, then saw holy ones receive an everlasting kingdom in night visions.
I studied Jeremiah's 70 years, then received a further timetable of 70 weeks until Messiah the Leader.
I warned Nebuchadnezzar he would dwell with beasts; later I charged Belshazzar with knowing that history and still exalting himself.
After weeks of mourning by the Tigris, I learned angelic opposition had delayed the answer from the first day I humbled myself.
I was told to seal the book until the time of the end, yet Jesus later cited my desolation prophecy for his disciples.
Scripture set my righteousness beside Noah and Job, and my wisdom was used in a rebuke directed to the ruler of Tyre.
I served from Nebuchadnezzar's court through Belshazzar's fall into the reigns of Darius and Cyrus.
I received dream-insight as a youth, then had night visions of my own that left me pale and alarmed.
Opponents trapped me with a Medo-Persian ban that could not be annulled, knowing only my worship of God could accuse me.
I heard that from the removal of the constant feature and the placing of the disgusting thing that causes desolation there would be 1,290 days.
I received the kingdom after Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed.
I was about 62 years old when I received the kingdom.
I appointed 120 satraps over the whole kingdom.
Daniel was one of my three high officials.
I intended to elevate Daniel over the entire kingdom.
I signed a decree that for 30 days petitions could be made only to me.
I had Daniel thrown into the pit of lions.
At dawn I hurried to the lions' pit and called out to Daniel.
I was made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans.
I was the son of Ahasuerus.
I was a descendant of the Medes.
The satraps were to report to my high officials so I would not suffer loss.
High officials and satraps came as a group and asked me to establish a royal ban.
They told me the law of the Medes and the Persians cannot be annulled.
When I heard Daniel had prayed, I was greatly distressed.
Until sunset I made every effort to save Daniel.
I told Daniel his God whom he continually served would rescue him.
I sealed the pit with my signet ring and with the signet rings of my nobles.
I passed the night fasting and could not sleep.
I asked whether Daniel's God had been able to rescue him from the lions.
I was overjoyed and commanded that Daniel be lifted out of the pit.
I ordered Daniel's accusers thrown into the lions' pit with their sons and wives.
Daniel prospered in my kingdom and in the kingdom of Cyrus the Persian.
In my first year Daniel discerned from the books Jeremiah's 70 years for Jerusalem.
I wrote to peoples, nations, and language groups throughout the earth.
I ordered that in every domain of my kingdom people tremble before the God of Daniel.
I said Daniel's God is the living God who endures forever.
I said his kingdom will never be destroyed and his rulership is eternal.
I said he rescues, saves, and performs signs and wonders, for he rescued Daniel from the paw of the lions.
In my first year an angel stood up to strengthen and fortify me.
After Belshazzar fell, I received the Chaldean kingdom at about 62, of Median descent, son of Ahasuerus.
Tricked into an unchangeable ban, I spent a sleepless night, then found Daniel unharmed and praised his God throughout my realm.
I set Daniel among three high officials over 120 satraps, meant to elevate him over all, then threw him to lions under my own sealed decree.
I was an Ethiopian in the king's house.
I was a eunuch in the king's house.
I heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern.
I went out and spoke to King Zedekiah about Jeremiah.
I pulled Jeremiah up out of the cistern.
Jehovah promised I would have my life as a spoil.
King Zedekiah was sitting in the Gate of Benjamin when I went to him.
I told King Zedekiah what had been done to Jeremiah the prophet was evil.
I said Jeremiah would die in the cistern because of the famine.
I said there was no bread left in the city.
King Zedekiah commanded me to take 30 men and pull Jeremiah up before he died.
I went beneath the treasury and took worn-out rags and pieces of cloth.
I let the rags and cloth down by ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern.
I told Jeremiah to put the rags between his armpits and the ropes.
After we drew him up, Jeremiah remained in the Courtyard of the Guard.
While Jeremiah was confined in the Courtyard of the Guard, Jehovah sent Jeremiah a word for me.
Jehovah said I would see his words of calamity fulfilled on the city.
Jehovah said I would not be handed over to the men I feared.
Jehovah said I would not fall by the sword.
Jehovah said he would surely provide me with escape.
Jehovah said I trusted in him.
From the king's house I protested Jeremiah's confinement in the cistern, got 30 men, padded the ropes with rags, and hauled him out.
Jehovah promised that when Jerusalem's calamity came, I would escape the sword because I trusted in him.
An Ethiopian court official, I spoke against the princes' cruelty and became Jeremiah the prophet's rescuer.
I became queen instead of Vashti.
I was a Jewish woman in Shushan the citadel.
Mordecai took me as his daughter.
I went in to Ahasuerus against the law to plead for my people.
Ahasuerus held out to me the golden scepter.
I invited Ahasuerus and Haman to a banquet I prepared.
I told Ahasuerus the adversary and enemy was evil Haman.
I asked that my life and my people be granted as my petition.
Ahasuerus gave me the house of Haman.
I helped establish the days of Purim among the Jews.
I was the daughter of Abihail, Mordecai's uncle.
I had neither father nor mother when Mordecai took me.
I was beautifully formed and attractive in appearance.
I was taken to the king's house under Hegai's care.
I did not say anything about my people or relatives.
Mordecai had instructed me not to tell anyone.
Hegai promptly arranged my beauty treatments and diet.
Hegai assigned me seven selected young women from the king's house.
When my turn came, I requested only what Hegai recommended.
I was taken to Ahasuerus in the tenth month, Tebeth, in his seventh year.
Ahasuerus put the royal headdress on my head.
Ahasuerus held a great banquet in my honor.
I spoke to Ahasuerus in Mordecai's name about a plot against him.
When I heard Mordecai was in sackcloth, I was deeply distressed.
I sent garments for Mordecai, but he refused them.
I sent Hathach to find out from Mordecai what was happening.
I said I had not been summoned to Ahasuerus for 30 days.
I said anyone entering the inner courtyard unsummoned faces death unless the golden scepter is held out.
I told Mordecai to gather the Jews in Shushan to fast for three days.
I said my female attendants and I would also fast.
I said, “If I am to perish, I will perish.”
On the third day I put on my royal robes and stood in the inner courtyard.
I approached and touched the top of the scepter.
I asked Ahasuerus and Haman to come again to a banquet the next day.
At the second banquet I said we had been sold to be annihilated, killed, and destroyed.
I fell at the king's feet and wept, pleading for my people.
I asked for an order to annul Haman's documents against the Jews.
I put Mordecai in charge of the house of Haman.
I revealed to Ahasuerus how Mordecai was related to me.
I asked that the Jews in Shushan act a second day according to the law.
I asked that the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the stake.
I continued to do what Mordecai said even after I became queen.
I was winning the favor of everyone who saw me.
Mordecai day after day walked before the courtyard to learn about my welfare.
I completed the prescribed 12-month beauty treatment before going in to Ahasuerus.
I told Ahasuerus that if my people had only been sold as slaves, I would have kept silent.
I said the distress was not proper, for it would be damaging to Ahasuerus.
Haman stood up to plead with me for his life.
Ahasuerus saw Haman thrown on the couch where I was.
I asked how I could bear to look upon the disaster coming on my people.
With Mordecai I wrote with full authority to confirm a second letter about Purim.
My command confirmed the matters concerning Purim, and it was recorded in a book.
I instructed observance of Purim including fasting and supplication.
When I came in before Ahasuerus, he ordered Haman's evil scheme to come back on his own head.
Orphaned cousin raised by Mordecai, I hid my people until I risked death to expose Haman's annihilation decree.
Twice I banqueted Ahasuerus and Haman, then named Haman before receiving his house and placing Mordecai over it.
After Haman fell, I wept for a counter-decree, won a second day in Shushan, and with Mordecai established Purim.
Unsummoned for 30 days, I fasted three days, touched the golden scepter, and said if I perish, I perish.
I was a priest and a copyist of the Law.
I came up from Babylon to Jerusalem.
King Artaxerxes granted everything I requested.
I read aloud the book of the Law before the people.
I led former exiles who had married foreign women to send them away.
I prepared my heart to consult Jehovah's Law, practice it, and teach it in Israel.
I was the son of Seraiah, a descendant of Aaron the chief priest.
I was well-versed in the Law of Moses.
I began the journey from Babylon on the first day of the first month.
I arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month.
Artaxerxes sent me with his seven advisers to investigate whether God's Law was being applied.
I praised Jehovah for putting it into the king's heart to beautify Jehovah's house.
I took courage because Jehovah's hand was upon me.
I assembled the travelers at the river that comes to Ahava.
At Ahava I found no Levites among the people and priests.
I sent for ministers from Iddo at Casiphia.
I proclaimed a fast at the river Ahava to seek guidance for our journey.
I was ashamed to ask Artaxerxes for soldiers and horsemen for protection.
We fasted and made request of our God, and he listened.
I weighed out silver, gold, and utensils to 12 chiefs of the priests.
Jehovah's hand rescued us from the enemy and from ambush along the way.
When I heard of foreign marriages, I ripped my garment and pulled out hair of my head and beard.
I sat in shock until the evening grain offering.
I got down on my knees and spread out my hands to Jehovah.
I said I felt ashamed and embarrassed to raise my face to God.
While I prayed and lay prostrate, a large crowd gathered weeping.
I had the chiefs of the priests, Levites, and all Israel take an oath.
I ate no food and drank no water, mourning over the unfaithfulness.
I stood on a wooden podium and opened the book in the sight of all the people.
As I opened the book, all the people stood up.
I praised Jehovah, and the people answered “Amen! Amen!”
I went before a thanksgiving choir at the inauguration of Jerusalem's wall.
My genealogy runs through Phinehas and Eleazar to Aaron.
I came in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
I told the holy vessels' guardians to weigh them out in Jehovah's house in Jerusalem.
On the fourth day in Jerusalem we weighed the silver and gold in God's house.
Princes told me the holy offspring had become mingled with the peoples of the lands.
I went to the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib while fasting.
I rose and told the people to separate from foreign wives.
In heavy rain the men of Judah and Benjamin sat in the courtyard before God's house at my summons.
With family heads I looked into the foreign-wife cases from the tenth month to the first.
I read from daybreak until midday before the Water Gate.
On the second day heads of houses gathered around me for further insight into the Law.
From that reading under my teaching the people learned to dwell in booths in the seventh month.
I served in the days of Nehemiah the governor as priest and copyist.
Copyist from Aaron's line, I left Babylon in Artaxerxes' seventh year without a military escort, trusting Jehovah's hand at Ahava.
I tore hair and clothes over mixed marriages, then led an oath and months-long inquiry to send the foreign wives away.
At the Water Gate I opened Moses' Law from daybreak to midday; the people wept, then rejoiced and kept booths as written.
Sent to beautify Jehovah's house and teach his Law, I later walked ahead of Jerusalem's wall thanksgiving choir as copyist.
The king of Babylon appointed me over the people left in Judah.
I was the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan.
I stayed at Mizpah.
I told the people to live in the land and serve the king of Babylon.
Ishmael struck me down with the sword at Mizpah.
Jeremiah came and stayed with me among the people left in the land.
Nebuzaradan handed Jeremiah over to me to be brought to my house.
Army chiefs came to me at Mizpah when they heard of my appointment.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah was among those who came to me.
Johanan son of Kareah also came to me with the army chiefs.
I swore an oath that they should not be afraid of serving the Chaldeans.
I said I would stay in Mizpah to represent them to the Chaldeans who came.
I told them to gather wine, summer fruits, and oil into storage.
Jews returned from Moab, Ammon, Edom, and other lands to me at Mizpah.
Under my care the people gathered wine and summer fruits in very great quantity.
Johanan warned me that Baalis king of the Ammonites had sent Ishmael to kill me.
I did not believe Johanan's warning.
Johanan secretly offered to strike Ishmael down for me.
I told Johanan not to do it, saying his report about Ishmael was a lie.
Nebuzaradan told Jeremiah he could return to me, whom Babylon's king had appointed over Judah's cities.
I was appointed over the men, women, and children from the poor left in the land.
Ishmael was of the royal line when he came to eat with me.
Ishmael and ten men rose up against me while we were eating a meal together.
I was put to death in the seventh month.
Chaldean soldiers with me in Mizpah were also struck down.
After my death the remnant feared the Chaldeans and headed toward Egypt.
Son of Ahikam, I governed Judah's remnant at Mizpah, urged service to Babylon, and hosted Jeremiah.
Warned that Baalis had sent Ishmael to kill me, I called it a lie and forbade Johanan's preemptive strike.
In the seventh month, while eating with Ishmael of the royal line, I was slain as the governor Babylon had appointed.
I was the Agagite enemy of the Jews in Esther's day.
King Ahasuerus put my throne above all the other princes.
I sought to annihilate all the Jews in the king's realm.
I had a stake put up for Mordecai.
I was hanged on the stake I prepared for Mordecai.
I was the son of Hammedatha.
When Mordecai would not bow to me, I became filled with rage.
I despised doing away with Mordecai alone.
Pur, that is, the Lot, was cast before me.
I offered Ahasuerus 10,000 silver talents for destroying a people.
Ahasuerus gave me his signet ring.
Queen Esther invited only me to accompany Ahasuerus to her banquet.
My wife's name was Zeresh.
I told Ahasuerus a certain people had laws different from all others.
Writing went out according to all I commanded, sealed with the king's signet ring.
I ordered annihilation of the Jews on the 13th day of Adar.
After the decree, Ahasuerus and I sat down to drink while Shushan was in confusion.
I boasted to my friends of my wealth, my many sons, and my promotion.
Nothing satisfied me while Mordecai the Jew sat in the king's gate.
Zeresh and my friends told me to have a stake put up 50 cubits high.
I came to ask Ahasuerus to hang Mordecai on the stake I had prepared.
I thought the man Ahasuerus wished to honor must be me.
Ahasuerus ordered me to honor Mordecai the Jew with attire and a horse.
I hurried home mourning with my head covered.
My wise men and Zeresh said I would surely fall before Mordecai.
Esther named me the adversary and enemy before Ahasuerus.
The king found me fallen on Esther's couch while I was pleading for my life.
From Nisan casting of Pur before me to Adar, I set one day to destroy every Jew in Ahasuerus's realm.
I proposed royal attire and the king's horse for the man Ahasuerus wished to honor, then had to lead Mordecai through the public square myself.
Harbona told Ahasuerus my 50-cubit stake still stood at my house, and Ahasuerus hung me on it.
After I fell, Ahasuerus gave my house to Esther and my former signet ring to Mordecai.
Purim recalls that I cast Pur against the Jews and that my evil scheme came back on my own head.
I was a companion of Daniel in Babylon.
With Mishael and Azariah, I refused to worship the image of gold.
King Nebuchadnezzar had me thrown into the burning fiery furnace.
Together with Mishael and Azariah, I stepped out of the fire unharmed.
I was among youths from Judah taken for the king's service.
The principal court official gave me a Babylonian name.
For ten days my companions and I ate vegetables and drank water instead of the king's delicacies.
At Daniel's request, Nebuchadnezzar appointed me over the administration of the province of Babylon.
Some Chaldeans accused me before Nebuchadnezzar of refusing his image.
With Mishael and Azariah I told Nebuchadnezzar that we had no need to answer him in that matter.
After three years of training, Nebuchadnezzar found no one like Daniel, Mishael, Azariah, and me.
In matters of wisdom, Nebuchadnezzar found my companions and me ten times better than his magic-practicing priests and conjurers.
When the wise men were to be killed, Daniel informed me and asked us to pray for mercy.
Mighty men bound me and my companions and threw us into the furnace still wearing our clothes.
The furnace was heated seven times hotter because of Mishael, Azariah, and me.
Not a hair of my head was singed, and there was not even the smell of fire on me.
With Mishael and Azariah I answered that God could rescue us from the furnace and from Nebuchadnezzar's hand.
With Mishael and Azariah I said that even if our God did not rescue us, we would not worship the image.
The men who took me up were killed by the flames, but I fell bound into the fire and later walked out free.
After the fire had no effect on my body or cloaks, Nebuchadnezzar promoted me again in the province of Babylon.
From Judah's youths in the palace school to administrators of Babylon, I stood with Mishael and Azariah against the golden image on the plain of Dura.
I was high priest after the exile.
I returned with Zerubbabel.
With Zerubbabel I built the altar of the God of Israel.
Jehovah stirred my spirit to work on His house.
In a vision I stood before the angel of Jehovah as high priest.
I was the son of Jehozadak.
Haggai spoke Jehovah's word to Zerubbabel and to me.
I listened to Haggai and began to show fear because of Jehovah.
With Zerubbabel I refused outsiders a share in building Jehovah's house.
With Zerubbabel I started again to rebuild God's house in Jerusalem.
Satan stood at my right hand to resist me.
I was clothed in filthy garments before the angel of Jehovah.
A clean turban was put on my head.
In the second year after the return, Zerubbabel and I appointed Levites as supervisors over Jehovah's house.
Haggai told me to be strong and work, for Jehovah of armies was with us.
The angel of Jehovah said my error had been caused to pass away and I would be clothed with fine garments.
I was told that if I walked in Jehovah's ways I would serve as a judge in His house.
Jehovah called me and my companions men who serve as a sign.
A stone with seven eyes was set before me.
Silver and gold were made into a crown and put on my head.
I became father to Joiakim.
Some of my sons were among priests who had taken foreign wives.
From the first altar with Zerubbabel to restarting the temple under Haggai and Zechariah, I led priestly restoration after exile.

After filthy garments were removed, Jehovah promised to bring His servant Sprout while I and my companions sat as a sign.

I raised Esther as my daughter.
I refused to bow low to Haman.
I uncovered a plot against King Ahasuerus.
Haman built a stake to hang me.
Ahasuerus made me second only to himself.
I was a Jew of Benjamin in Shushan the citadel.
Esther was the daughter of my father's brother.
I instructed Esther not to reveal her people.
Day after day I walked before the courtyard of the house of the women to learn about Esther.
I sat in the king's gate.
While refusing to bow, I told them that I was a Jew.
I put on sackcloth and ashes and cried out loudly in the city.
I sent Esther a copy of the decree and told her to plead with Ahasuerus.
Ahasuerus ordered Haman to clothe me and lead me on the king's horse.
Esther put me in charge of Haman's house.
I was son of Jair son of Shimei son of Kish.
My family line went back to Kish, who was associated with Jeconiah's exile.
Bigthan and Teresh plotted while I sat in the king's gate, and I told Queen Esther.
I would not accept the garments Esther sent in place of my sackcloth.
I told Esther that relief for the Jews would come from another source if she remained silent.
I asked who knows whether she attained royal status for a time like this.
After being honored, I returned to the king's gate while Haman hurried home mourning.
I wrote in the king's name and sealed documents with his signet ring for the Jews.
I left Ahasuerus's presence in royal apparel of blue and white, wearing a great golden crown.
I recorded the events and instructed the Jews to observe the 14th and 15th of Adar.
With Esther I wrote with full authority to confirm Purim.
From a Benjaminite family affected by Jeconiah's exile, I worked for the good of my people in Shushan.
I would not bow to Haman, then later rode the king's horse while Haman called out my honor.
I charged Esther to go in to Ahasuerus, then carried out her order to gather the Jews of Shushan to fast.
Princes and satraps supported the Jews because they feared me as I grew steadily more powerful.
I sealed a decree allowing the Jews to defend their lives on the 13th of Adar, the day Haman had chosen for their destruction.
I was king of Babylon.
I besieged Jerusalem.
I took utensils from Jehovah's house to Babylon.
I carried people of Judah into exile.
I destroyed Jerusalem and burned Jehovah's house.
I had a dream that left me agitated and unable to sleep.
I demanded that my wise men tell me both the dream and its interpretation.
I made an image of gold and set it up on the plain of Dura.
I ordered that whoever would not worship my image be thrown into the burning fiery furnace.
I ordered Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego thrown into the furnace.
I saw four men walking free in the midst of the fire.
I was driven away from mankind and ate vegetation like bulls.
After my understanding returned, I praised the Most High.
Jehovah called me his servant.
Jehoiakim became my servant, then rebelled against me.
In Jehoiakim's third year I came to Jerusalem and besieged it.
I brought temple utensils to the land of Shinar, to the house of my god.
I ordered Ashpenaz to bring youths of royal and noble descent for my service.
I assigned the youths daily rations from my delicacies and wine and had them trained for three years.
When I spoke with the youths, I found none like Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
In matters of wisdom I found four Hebrews ten times better than my magic-practicing priests and conjurers.
In my second year I summoned magic-practicing priests, conjurers, sorcerers, and Chaldeans about my dreams.
I threatened to dismember my wise men and turn their houses into public latrines if they failed.
I flew into a violent rage and ordered all the wise men of Babylon destroyed.
I fell facedown and paid homage to Daniel, saying his God is a God of gods and a Revealer of secrets.
I elevated Daniel and made him ruler over the province of Babylon.
At Daniel's request I appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over Babylon's administration.
My golden image was 60 cubits high and 6 cubits wide.
I assembled satraps, prefects, governors, and administrators for the inauguration of my image.
In a furious rage I ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter than usual.
The men who took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego for me were killed by the flames.
I said the fourth man in the fire looked like a son of the gods.
I called the three out of the furnace as servants of the Most High God.
I ordered that anyone speaking against their God be dismembered.
I promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
I dreamed of an enormous tree whose top reached the heavens.
I saw a watcher, a holy one, come down and call for the tree to be chopped down.
Twelve months after the dream, I was walking on the roof of my palace in Babylon.
I said, “Is this not Babylon the Great that I myself have built?”
While that boast was still in my mouth, a voice from the heavens said my kingdom had gone away from me.
My hair grew long like eagles' feathers and my nails like birds' claws.
I took Jehoiachin captive in the eighth year of my reign.
I made Mattaniah king in Jehoiachin's place and changed his name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah rebelled against me after I had made him take an oath by God.
I came with all my army against Jerusalem and built a siege wall all around it.
At Riblah I blinded Zedekiah after his sons were slaughtered before his eyes.
I appointed Gedaliah over the people left in the land of Judah.
I ordered Nebuzaradan to look after Jeremiah, do him no harm, and grant whatever he asked.
I named Daniel Belteshazzar after the name of my god.
I made Daniel chief of the magic-practicing priests.
I told Belteshazzar that no secret was too difficult for him.
My wise men could not interpret the tree dream even after I told them what I had dreamed.
I said I was at ease in my house and prospering in my palace when the tree dream came.
After seven times passed over me, my understanding returned when I looked up to the heavens.
My high officials and nobles eagerly sought me out, and even more greatness was added to me.
I declared that the Most High is able to humiliate those who walk in pride.
I asked who is the god who could rescue the three Hebrews out of my hands.
I praised the God who sent his angel and rescued his servants who trusted in him.
I cut into pieces the gold utensils Solomon had made in Jehovah's temple.
I took about 10,000 into exile from Jerusalem, leaving the poorest of the land.
In my 19th year Nebuzaradan my chief of the guard came to Jerusalem.
At Riblah in the land of Hamath I struck down and put to death leading men brought from Jerusalem.
I took from Egypt's king everything from the Wadi of Egypt up to the Euphrates River.
I came up against Jehoiakim to bind him with two copper fetters to take him to Babylon.
Jeremiah said Jehovah had given all those lands into my hand, even the wild beasts of the field.
Jeremiah said the nations would serve me and my son and my grandson.
Jehovah said he was sending for me, his servant, against Judah and the surrounding nations.
I made my army labor greatly against Tyre, yet we received no wages from that labor.
Jehovah said he was giving me the land of Egypt as wages for my army.
Jehovah said he was bringing me against Tyre from the north as a king of kings.
Jehovah said he would place my throne above the stones Jeremiah hid at Tahpanhes.
Daniel told me I myself was the head of gold on the immense image in my dream.
I ordered the wise men destroyed over a dream I would not relate, then elevated the exile who told both dream and interpretation.
I took Jehovah's utensils to my god's treasury; later they were still known as what I had carried off from Jerusalem.
Jehovah said that after 70 years he would call my city Babylon to account.
I put Judah under covenant oath so it could stand only by serving me.
When Zedekiah broke that oath and looked to Egypt, I blinded him at Riblah and took him captive to Babylon.
I ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter, then praised the God who rescued the men I had thrown in.
I boasted of Babylon the Great on my palace roof; at that word I was driven to dwell with the beasts.
I was cupbearer to Artaxerxes.
I rebuilt the walls of Jerusalem.
I was governor in the land of Judah.
I served King Artaxerxes.
I wept when I heard that Jerusalem's walls were broken down.
I asked Artaxerxes to send me to Judah to rebuild the city.
I inspected Jerusalem's ruined walls at night.
I told the people, “Come, let us rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.”
Sanballat and Tobiah opposed my work.
I finished Jerusalem's wall in 52 days.
I stopped nobles from demanding interest from their brothers.
I threw Tobiah's furniture out of the temple storeroom.
I was the son of Hacaliah.
I was in Shushan the citadel when news came from Judah.
My brother Hanani brought me word about Jerusalem.
I fasted and prayed for days after hearing the bad news.
I had never been gloomy in the king's presence before.
Artaxerxes noticed my gloominess of heart.
I asked for letters to the governors Beyond the River.
I asked Artaxerxes for a letter directing Asaph to provide timber from the Royal Park.
Artaxerxes sent army chiefs and horsemen with me.
I stayed in Jerusalem three days before inspecting the city wall.
I did not tell anyone what my God had put into my heart to do.
I went out by night through the Valley Gate.
I told Sanballat he had neither share nor claim nor memorial in Jerusalem.
I posted families with swords, lances, and bows at the exposed places.
I told the people to remember Jehovah and fight for their families.
Half of my men worked while half held the weapons.
The one to blow the horn stood beside me.
I refused Sanballat's invitation to meet in the Valley Plain of Ono.
I said I was engaged in a great work and could not go down.
I would not run into the temple to save my life.
For 12 years I did not eat the food allowance due the governor.
I put my brother Hanani in charge of Jerusalem.
As governor I told the people not to mourn on the holy day.
The news reached me in the month of Chislev, in the 20th year.
I spoke to Artaxerxes in the month of Nisan, in his 20th year.
I confessed the sins of Israel, including my own and my father's house.
At the King's Pool there was not enough space for the animal I was riding.
I shook out the folds of my garment against anyone who broke the interest promise.
Former governors had taken 40 silver shekels a day for bread and wine, but I did not.
One hundred fifty Jews and deputy rulers ate at my table.
Sanballat's open letter accused me of planning to become king.
I saw that Tobiah and Sanballat had hired Shemaiah against me.
My wall was completed on the 25th day of Elul.
I found the book of genealogical enrollment of those who first came up.
I ordered Jerusalem's gates closed before the Sabbath.
I warned traders spending the night outside Jerusalem's wall that I would use force.
I pulled out the hair of men who had married foreign women.
I drove away Joiada's son, the son-in-law of Sanballat.
I went to Artaxerxes in his 32nd year, then returned on leave.
I sealed the written agreement first among the leaders.
From cupbearer in Shushan to governor of Judah, I rebuilt Jerusalem's wall my brother Hanani reported was broken down.
I inspected the ruined gates by night, then later closed Jerusalem's gates to keep the Sabbath holy.
I refused a meeting at Ono and refused to hide in the temple, while Tobiah kept sending letters to frighten me.
I stopped interest-taking among the nobles, then later threw an Ammonite official's furniture out of God's house.
After 12 years without taking the governor's food, I returned from Artaxerxes and found Eliashib had given Tobiah a storeroom.
I appointed Hanani over Jerusalem, then with Ezra calmed a weeping people on the day the Law was read.
Enemies mocked our half-built wall, yet we finished it in 52 days, and the nations saw it was done with God's help.
From night inspection with one animal to choirs on the finished wall, I led Judah from disgrace to dedication.
I became furious and greatly offended when I heard that the Jews were rebuilding the wall.
I was a Horonite.
I mocked the Jews who were rebuilding Jerusalem's wall.
I tried to stop the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall.
I was very displeased that someone had come to help Israel.
With Tobiah and Geshem, I mocked the builders and accused them of rebelling.
Before the army of Samaria I asked if the feeble Jews would finish in a day.
I conspired with others to fight against Jerusalem.
I invited Nehemiah to meet in the villages of the Valley Plain of Ono.
I sent Nehemiah the same meeting message four times.
On the fifth try I sent my attendant with an open letter.
My letter claimed Nehemiah was scheming to become king.
I claimed prophets were proclaiming, “There is a king in Judah!”
With Tobiah I hired Shemaiah to frighten Nehemiah.
One of Joiada's sons became my son-in-law.
From mocking “feeble Jews” before Samaria's army to an open letter naming Nehemiah a rebel king, I repeatedly tried to stop Jerusalem's wall.
I schemed harm at Ono, hired a false prophecy, and still saw Jerusalem's wall finished in 52 days.
After opposing the rebuild, my family tie into the high priest's house got Joiada's son driven away.
I opposed Nehemiah's work in Jerusalem.
I was an Ammonite official.
I mocked the Jews who were rebuilding Jerusalem's wall.
I tried to frighten Nehemiah with letters.
I was very displeased that someone had come to help Israel.
Standing beside Sanballat, I said a fox could knock down their stone wall.
I joined Sanballat and others in conspiring against Jerusalem.
With Sanballat I hired Shemaiah to speak a false prophecy.
Nobles of Judah kept sending me letters, and I replied.
I was a son-in-law of Shecaniah the son of Arah.
My son Jehohanan had married a daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah.
Many in Judah swore allegiance to me.
Eliashib the priest was a relative of mine.
While Nehemiah was away, Eliashib made a large temple storeroom available for me.
I mocked that a fox could topple their wall, then watched that wall finished in 52 days.
Through marriage ties in Judah I gained allies who praised me to Nehemiah while reporting his words back to me.
Nehemiah threw my household furniture out of the temple storeroom.
I was King Ahasuerus' queen.
I refused to come when Ahasuerus ordered me brought in.
I was very beautiful.
I held a banquet for the women at the royal house.
Ahasuerus wanted me brought wearing the royal headdress.
Seven court officials carried the king's order to me.
The king's rage flared up when I refused.
My refusal came on the seventh day of the king's banquet.
Memucan said I had done wrong not only against Ahasuerus but against all the princes and peoples.
A decree said that I may never again come in before King Ahasuerus.
Ahasuerus was to confer my royal position on a woman better than I.
After the king's rage subsided, he remembered what I had done.
From hosting the women's banquet to losing my royal place, one refusal ended my standing before Ahasuerus.
I was summoned to display my beauty in the royal headdress, and Esther later wore that headdress as queen instead of me.
My refusal led to an unrepealable Persian decree and a search for a queen to replace me.
I was among the leaders who brought exiles back from Babylon to Judah.
I helped rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.
I was governor of Judah.
I worked alongside Jeshua the high priest.
I was the son of Shealtiel.
With Jeshua I built the altar of the God of Israel.
In the second year after our return we started the work on Jehovah's house.
I refused to let surrounding peoples build the temple with us.
I told them they had no share with us in building a house to our God.
When Haggai prophesied, Jehovah stirred up my spirit to work on Jehovah's house.
I listened to the voice of Jehovah through Haggai the prophet.
The prophets of God were with me when I restarted the rebuilding.
Matthew lists me in the genealogy of Jesus after the deportation to Babylon.
Those who came with me included Jeshua, Nehemiah, and others named in the return list.
We set the altar on its former site despite fear of the surrounding peoples.
Adversaries claimed to me that they had sacrificed to our God since Esar-haddon's day.
Haggai addressed me as governor while the people lived in paneled houses and Jehovah's house lay in ruins.
Jehovah told me through Haggai, “Be strong… and work.”
Jehovah said he would make me like a seal ring because he had chosen me.
Jehovah's word to me said, “Not by a military force, nor by power, but by my spirit.”
My hands laid the foundation of Jehovah's house, and my hands would finish it.
I refused the surrounding peoples who asked to join the work, citing Cyrus's command.
Under Darius, I restarted Jehovah's house with Haggai and Zechariah.
I laid the temple's foundation amid mixed weeping and shouting, then later held the plumb line as the work moved beyond small beginnings.
As governor of Judah and Jehovah's chosen seal ring, I stand in Matthew's line from Jeconiah toward the Christ.
Before me a great mountain was to become level land, and I would bring out the top stone amid shouts of wonder.
